---
title: "Combining NixOS and Home Manager"
---

# Combining NixOS and Home Manager

Managing NixOS system configurations and Home Manager user environments separately creates two different rebuild workflows. The boring default is: **import Home Manager as a NixOS module inside `configuration.nix` so a single `nixos-rebuild switch` updates the OS, system services, and user dotfiles atomically**.

## Mental model

By importing `home-manager.nixosModules.home-manager`:
- System configuration and user environments share the same evaluation.
- `nixos-rebuild switch` updates both the system packages and all user dotfiles in one command.
- System rollbacks automatically restore both system state and user dotfile state in unison.

```
configuration.nix
      ├── Systemd services, kernel, hardware
      └── home-manager.users.deskuser = {
            # User dotfiles, git settings, personal shell
          };
```

## Worked examples

Save as `unified.nix`:

```nix
# unified.nix
{ config, pkgs, ... }:

{
  # In your NixOS configuration.nix:
  # imports = [ <home-manager/nixos> ];

  home-manager.useGlobalPkgs = true;
  home-manager.useUserPackages = true;

  home-manager.users.deskadmin = { pkgs, ... }: {
    home.stateVersion = "24.11";
    programs.git.enable = true;
  };
}
```

Setting `useGlobalPkgs = true;` prevents Home Manager from evaluating a second copy of `nixpkgs`, speeding up evaluation and saving disk space.

## The boring rule

- Integrate Home Manager into NixOS using `home-manager.nixosModules.home-manager`.
- Set `home-manager.useGlobalPkgs = true;`.
- Enjoy single-command atomic updates for host OS and user space simultaneously.
